classical_dev_results_note: CPU classical baselines were scored on dev seeds before any GPU dev result existed; they do not alter the frozen selection rule.

compute.budget_note: wall clock on one GPU including inference; learners stop gracefully

development_rounds.classical: plans/classical.json (28 CPU jobs, dev seeds 2026092301 and 2026092302).
development_rounds.round1: plans/candidates.draft.json -> plans/dev1.json (36 jobs, seed 2026092301, levels 1000/10000); 4x-0.5 normalization; 3 jobs ran on 2 GPUs, the rest on 8.
development_rounds.round2: plans/candidates_b.json (executed 4-candidate subset of plans/candidates_b_full.json) -> plans/dev1b.json (8 jobs, 4 GPUs); per-feature standardized MLPs and a batch-250 transductive Ladder.
development_rounds.second_dev_seed_note: The frozen rule allowed a second dev seed for the top five GPU candidates if the budget permitted; after round 1 the upper-envelope ledger had $8.78 left, so GPU candidates have one dev seed and the CPU kernel candidates have two.

disclosures: The literature-research agent ran informal single-draw CPU pilots (kernel ridge, MLP variants, VAT, SVM, kNN) on dataset seed 2026092001, which is one of the eleven FINAL seeds, using its query labels through a throwaway local script. Those pilots informed the candidate list, not the selection rule; the formal selection uses only dev seeds. This is a mild contamination of one final draw at the level of recipe design and is disclosed here.
The classical-baseline builder scored its CPU baselines on dev seeds 2026092301/2026092302 with a throwaway script while developing; no final-seed labels were used.

The first two smoke apps failed inside the container because block_network=True prevented Modal blob-store transfers; no learner output was produced; the ledger charged an upper-envelope $0.13 for them.

Modal sometimes serves an NVIDIA A100 80GB PCIe when A100-40GB is requested (observed in the smoke stage, as in the earlier nine-a100-throughput study). The ledger charges the published A100-40GB rate ($0.00065316 per worker-second) for every second of app lifetime with both workers assumed busy; the report adds a separate note on the at most ~6% rate difference. The ledger is an upper-envelope estimate, not a provider invoice.

Development round 1 (2026-09-23/24, dev seed 2026092301): all four VAT arms (input_noise_std 1.2 in 4x-0.5 units, eps 2-4.5, 600 epochs) scored ~90% error (constant class). A CPU reproduction of the exact config (1200x1200, single member) reproduced the collapse by epoch 100: training loss on NOISED inputs fell to 0.47 while error on CLEAN training inputs was 89.7%, i.e. the network learned the noisy-input regime only. Short CPU runs (20 epochs) and configs without the 4x-scaled noise train normally. The cause is the noise-unit conversion error (the pilot used per-feature standardized inputs with noise 0.3 SD), amplified by VAT and long training; it is not a CUDA or VAT-implementation defect. VAT with standardized inputs was drafted for round 2 but dropped for budget; it is untested here.

draws.disjointness: query rows are disjoint from every training prefix (n <= 10000)
draws.final_seed_note: the same eleven seeds as mnist/experiments/cutoff-calibration-20260920, enabling a paired comparison against its spatial CNN results
draws.nesting: training prefixes are nested across levels within a dataset seed
draws.rule: order = Generator(PCG64(SeedSequence(seed).spawn(2)[0])).permutation(60000); train = order[:n] (nested prefixes across levels); query = order[10000:20000]
draws.stage_seed_binding: 'smoke' and 'dev' jobs may only use dev seeds and 'final' jobs only final seeds; study.make_job refuses other combinations and score.py refuses to read query labels for a job whose stage and seed disagree

features.permutation_disclosure: Learners never receive perm, its inverse, pixel coordinates, or any spatial metadata. Recovering topology from the data itself is allowed and must be declared by the candidate.
features.permutation_rule: perm = np.random.Generator(np.random.PCG64(20260923)).permutation(81); every train and query image is presented as x[:, perm]
features.resize: uint8 -> float32/255; canonical_data.area_resize exact separable box-area averaging 28->9; np.clip to [0,1]; flatten row-major to 81 features (f=row*9+col)

learner_contract.api: learners.fit_predict(train_x, train_y, query_x, config, seed, deadline_unix, device)
forbidden: any pretrained weights or external data
learner_contract.transductive_rule: unlabeled use of query_x is allowed and must be recorded per candidate as 'uses_query_images_unlabeled'

outputs.predictions: predictions/<job_id>.npz with logits float32 (10000,10) and labels uint8 (10000,)
outputs.tie_break: labels = argmax over logits with ties resolved to the lowest class index

prediction_freeze: final scoring requires predictions/final_freeze.json covering every planned final job id; score.py refuses to score an unfrozen or altered final run, requires every planned job to have a result even for a --job-id spot check (which writes results/scores_final_filtered.json, never the canonical table), marks the freeze 'scored' once final labels have been read and then refuses any re-freeze; superseding an unscored freeze needs --refreeze and archives the previous file
question: Best achievable permutation-invariant accuracy under 1200 s on one A100-40GB per fit, and a five-level ladder from 1,000 to 10,000 training examples.

selection_rule.bottom_of_ladder: The same rule applied at N=1000. If the N=1000 winner differs from the N=10000 winner, both recipes are measured on the final draws at all five levels and the ladder reports the per-level minimum with the recipe identified.
selection_rule.budget_fallback: If the projected final cost of a winner exceeds the remaining authorized allowance, the next-best eligible candidate whose projected cost fits is used instead, and the substitution is disclosed in the report.
selection_rule.dev_evidence: Query error on dev seed 2026092301 at N=1000 and N=10000 for every candidate in plans/candidates.draft.json (GPU) and plans/classical_candidates.json (CPU); a second dev seed (2026092302) is run for the top five candidates at each N if the budget permits, and the mean over available dev seeds is used.
selection_rule.eligibility: A candidate is eligible at a level only if every dev fit at that level finished untruncated within the 1200 s per-fit budget on one A100-40GB (classical CPU fits: within 1200 s wall on the controller CPU).
selection_rule.final_measurement: Selected recipe(s) are retrained from scratch on every final seed 2026092001..2026092011 at every level 1000, 1778, 3162, 5623, 10000 with learner seed 11; all predictions are frozen (predictions/final_freeze.json) before score.py reads any final query label.
selection_rule.no_test_guided_changes: No recipe hyperparameter, epoch count, member count or checkpoint is changed after final query labels are read.
selection_rule.top_of_ladder: The recipe with the lowest mean dev error at N=10000 among eligible candidates; ties within 0.05 percentage points go to the recipe with lower mean fit wall time.
selection_rule.two_ladders: Results are reported separately for (A) dense-only permutation-invariant recipes (families mlp, ladder, classical) and (B) unrestricted permutation-invariant recipes, which additionally admit data-driven pixel-topology recovery followed by a convolutional learner (family topo_cnn). The choice between A and B is a competition-rules decision for the user, not a result of this study.

source.pool: official MNIST 60,000-example training split (no official test split is used)
